10		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
11	)
12	
13	// snapshotVersionRegisterRequest is the body of the collection POST: the
14	// calling device, the stable version name to create and the existing snapshot
15	// cursor it is bound to.
16	type snapshotVersionRegisterRequest struct {
17		DeviceID       string          `json:"deviceId"`
18		Name           string          `json:"name"`
19		SnapshotCursor json.RawMessage `json:"snapshotCursor"`
20	}
21	
22	// snapshotVersionBindRequest is the body of the rename (PUT
23	// .../snapshots/versions/{name}): the calling device and the existing
24	// snapshot cursor the name is moved onto. The name itself is in the path.
25	type snapshotVersionBindRequest struct {
26		DeviceID       string          `json:"deviceId"`
27		SnapshotCursor json.RawMessage `json:"snapshotCursor"`
28	}
29	
30	// snapshotVersionRestoreRequest is the body of the by-name restore: the
31	// calling device and the change id the restored state is appended under. The
32	// source snapshot is named by the path rather than carried in the body.
33	type snapshotVersionRestoreRequest struct {
34		DeviceID string `json:"deviceId"`
35		ChangeID string `json:"changeId"`
36	}
37	
38	// snapshotVersionItem fixes the on-the-wire key order of one list entry to
39	// name then snapshotCursor.
40	type snapshotVersionItem struct {
41		Name   string `json:"name"`
42		Cursor int64  `json:"snapshotCursor"`
43	}
44	
45	// snapshotVersionListResponse is the list body with the top-level key order
46	// fixed to versions then count; Versions is always a non-nil slice so an
47	// empty view serializes as [].
48	type snapshotVersionListResponse struct {
49		Versions []snapshotVersionItem `json:"versions"`
50		Count    int                   `json:"count"`
51	}
52	
53	// decodeVersionBindRequest enforces the rename endpoint's JSON shape:
54	// application/json body with a non-empty deviceId and a positive-integer
55	// snapshotCursor. Every violation is a 400 JSON error and the caller returns
56	// without touching the store.
57	func decodeVersionBindRequest(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (deviceID string, cursor int64, ok bool) {
58		var req snapshotVersionBindRequest
59		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
60			return "", 0, false
61		}
62		if req.DeviceID == "" {
63			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
64			return "", 0, false
65		}
66		// snapshotCursor must be present and a positive integer (no fractions,
67		// strings, booleans, null or zero).
68		if len(req.SnapshotCursor) == 0 {
69			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "snapshotCursor must be a positive integer")
70			return "", 0, false
71		}
72		c, good := parsePositiveInt(req.SnapshotCursor)
73		if !good {
74			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "snapshotCursor must be a positive integer")
75			return "", 0, false
76		}
77		return req.DeviceID, c, true
78	}
79	
80	// versionDeviceFromQuery resolves the calling device of a bodyless or
81	// read-only version endpoint from the deviceId query parameter. A missing or
82	// empty parameter is judged exactly like an unregistered device: a 404 JSON
83	// error ahead of any version or snapshot observation.
84	func versionDeviceFromQuery(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (string, bool) {
85		deviceID := r.URL.Query().Get("deviceId")
86		if deviceID == "" {
87			writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
88			return "", false
89		}
90		return deviceID, true
91	}
92	
93	// writeVersionGateError maps the shared gate/existence errors of every version
94	// endpoint onto their fixed status codes, returning true when err was handled.
95	// The order mirrors the verdict order: device existence (404), permission
96	// (403), version and snapshot existence (404), conflict (409); none of the
97	// failure bodies exposes version content.
98	func writeVersionGateError(w http.ResponseWriter, err error) bool {
99		var conflict *events.ErrVersionConflict
100		switch {
101		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
102			writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
103		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
104			writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
105		case errors.Is(err, events.ErrVersionNotFound):
106			writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "snapshot version not found")
107		case errors.Is(err, events.ErrSnapshotNotFound):
108			writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "snapshot not found")
109		case errors.As(err, &conflict):
110			writeJSON(w, http.StatusConflict, map[string]string{
111				"error":        "snapshot version is already bound to another cursor",
112				"conflictName": conflict.Name,
113			})
114		default:
115			return false
116		}
117		return true
118	}
119	
120	// handlePutSnapshotVersion registers an existing snapshot under a stable
121	// version name:
122	//
123	//	POST /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots/versions
124	//
125	// The name is unique within the document and travels in the JSON body.
126	// Binding the same name to the same cursor again is idempotent and returns the
127	// identical body; binding that name to another cursor (or a name another
128	// cursor occupies) is a 409 with zero writes. The fixed verdict order is
129	// request shape (400), device existence (404), document permission (403), then
130	// snapshot and version existence (404) and the conflict verdict (409). Success
131	// is one compact JSON line naming the version and the snapshot cursor.
132	func handlePutSnapshotVersion(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
133		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
134	
135		var req snapshotVersionRegisterRequest
136		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
137			return
138		}
139		if req.DeviceID == "" {
140			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
141			return
142		}
143		if req.Name == "" {
144			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "name must be a non-empty string")
145			return
146		}
147		// snapshotCursor must be present and a positive integer (no fractions,
148		// strings, booleans, null or zero).
149		if len(req.SnapshotCursor) == 0 {
150			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "snapshotCursor must be a positive integer")
151			return
152		}
153		cursor, ok := parsePositiveInt(req.SnapshotCursor)
154		if !ok {
155			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "snapshotCursor must be a positive integer")
156			return
157		}
158	
159		result, err := s.PutSnapshotVersion(documentID, req.DeviceID, req.Name, cursor)
160		if err != nil {
161			if !writeVersionGateError(w, err) {
162				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to register snapshot version")
163			}
164			return
165		}
166		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, result)
167	}
168	
169	// handleListSnapshotVersions is the read-only collection view:
170	//
171	//	GET /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots/versions?deviceId=D
172	//
173	// It returns every registration in ascending version-name order, each entry
174	// naming only the name and the snapshot cursor; an unknown document (or one
175	// without markers) reads as an empty array with count 0 rather than an error.
176	// The calling device must be registered (404) and still authorized (403); the
177	// read writes nothing and exposes no snapshot state.
178	func handleListSnapshotVersions(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
179		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
180	
181		deviceID, ok := versionDeviceFromQuery(w, r)
182		if !ok {
183			return
184		}
185	
186		versions, err := s.ListSnapshotVersions(documentID, deviceID)
187		if err != nil {
188			if !writeVersionGateError(w, err) {
189				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to list snapshot versions")
190			}
191			return
192		}
193	
194		items := make([]snapshotVersionItem, 0, len(versions))
195		for _, v := range versions {
196			items = append(items, snapshotVersionItem{Name: v.Name, Cursor: v.Cursor})
197		}
198		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, snapshotVersionListResponse{Versions: items, Count: len(items)})
199	}
200	
201	// handleGetSnapshotVersion reads the snapshot state a version name points at:
202	//
203	//	GET /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots/versions/{name}?deviceId=D
204	//
205	// The body is byte-for-byte the by-cursor snapshot read
206	// ({"cursor":N,"state":...}): the state is presented exactly as stored. The
207	// verdict order is shape (400), device existence (404), permission (403),
208	// version and snapshot existence (404).
209	func handleGetSnapshotVersion(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
210		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
211		name := r.PathValue("name")             // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
212	
213		deviceID, ok := versionDeviceFromQuery(w, r)
214		if !ok {
215			return
216		}
217	
218		cursor, state, err := s.GetSnapshotVersionState(documentID, deviceID, name)
219		if err != nil {
220			if !writeVersionGateError(w, err) {
221				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to load snapshot version")
222			}
223			return
224		}
225		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"cursor": cursor, "state": state})
226	}
227	
228	// handleRebindSnapshotVersion moves an existing version name onto another
229	// existing snapshot:
230	//
231	//	PUT /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots/versions/{name}
232	//
233	// The verdict order is request shape (400), device existence (404), permission
234	// (403), then the version marker (a missing name is 404) and the target
235	// snapshot (a missing cursor, an unknown document included, is 404). Rebinding
236	// to the cursor already bound is an idempotent no-op with the same body. The
237	// snapshot itself is never modified.
238	func handleRebindSnapshotVersion(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
239		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
240		name := r.PathValue("name")             // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
241	
242		deviceID, cursor, ok := decodeVersionBindRequest(w, r)
243		if !ok {
244			return
245		}
246	
247		result, err := s.RebindSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, name, cursor)
248		if err != nil {
249			if !writeVersionGateError(w, err) {
250				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to rename snapshot version")
251			}
252			return
253		}
254		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, result)
255	}
256	
257	// handleDeleteSnapshotVersion hard-deletes one version marker:
258	//
259	//	DELETE /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots/versions/{name}?deviceId=D
260	//
261	// The request carries no body. A missing marker is a 404 JSON error; the
262	// snapshot itself is untouched and, once the deletion commits, the name is
263	// free to bind again. Success is one compact JSON line naming the version and
264	// the deletion marker.

14	// sessionRestoreRequest is the session-scoped restore body: only the change
15	// id and the snapshot cursor travel in the request. The calling device is the
16	// session's owning device resolved from the path, so a stray deviceId is
17	// decoded and ignored like every other unknown field.
18	type sessionRestoreRequest struct {
19		ChangeID       string          `json:"changeId"`
20		SnapshotCursor json.RawMessage `json:"snapshotCursor"`
21	}

23	// handleSessionRestore is the session-scoped history restore, the session
24	// view's counterpart to POST /v1/documents/{documentID}/restore, mounted one
25	// segment below the session document resource:
26	//
27	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/restore
28	//
29	// The body carries only changeId and snapshotCursor; the calling device is the
30	// session's owning device resolved from the path with the same identity rule
31	// as the session reads, exports, commits, replays, merges, polls and
32	// subscriptions — no new credential is introduced, and a stray deviceId in the
33	// body is ignored like any other unknown field. On a snapshot hit the snapshot
34	// state is appended as one ordinary change in a single serialized transaction:
35	// old rows are untouched and the document cursor advances by one. The success
36	// body is byte-identical to the document-level restore: id, created, the
37	// assigned cursor and the source snapshot cursor. The checks run in the fixed
38	// order request shape (400), session existence (404), document permission
39	// (403) — the permission verdict is taken inside the restore transaction, so a
40	// revoked device writes nothing — followed by the snapshot lookup (a miss, an
41	// unknown document included, is 404) and the idempotency/conflict verdict (an
42	// id occupied by an ordinary change, or a restore whose device, snapshot
43	// cursor or source state differs, is 409). Every rejection leaves the log
44	// untouched.
45	func handleSessionRestore(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
46		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
47		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
48	
49		var req sessionRestoreRequest
50		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
51			return
52		}
53		if req.ChangeID == "" {
54			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "changeId must be a non-empty string")
55			return
56		}
57		// snapshotCursor must be present and a positive integer (no fractions,
58		// strings, booleans, null or zero).
59		if len(req.SnapshotCursor) == 0 {
60			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "snapshotCursor must be a positive integer")
61			return
62		}
63		snapshotCursor, ok := parsePositiveInt(req.SnapshotCursor)
64		if !ok {
65			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "snapshotCursor must be a positive integer")
66			return
67		}
68	
69		// Request shape is settled; only now does the session lookup run, so a
70		// malformed restore against an unknown session is still a 400.
71		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
72		if err != nil {
73			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
74				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
75				return
76			}
77			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
78			return
79		}
80	
81		result, err := s.RestoreSessionSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, req.ChangeID, snapshotCursor)
82		if err != nil {
83			var conflict *events.ErrRestoreConflict
84			switch {
85			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
86				// The session's device was deregistered between the lookup and the
87				// restore; its cascade removed the session too, so the identity the
88				// caller used no longer exists.
89				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
90			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
91				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
92			case errors.Is(err, events.ErrSnapshotNotFound):
93				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "snapshot not found")
94			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
95				writeJSON(w, http.StatusConflict, map[string]string{
96					"error":      "change id already exists with a different deviceId, snapshotCursor or source state",
97					"conflictId": conflict.ID,
98				})
99			default:
100				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to restore snapshot")
101			}
102			return
103		}
104	
105		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, result)
106	}

108	// malformedSessionRestorePath reports whether p targets the session-scoped
109	// restore endpoint but is not at its exact location
110	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/restore): a missing
111	// "documents" segment, an extra segment, or a "restore" segment in a position
112	// short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer those with a
113	// plain-text 404 (or a redirect for an empty segment); every failure of this
114	// endpoint must be a JSON 400 instead. Empty segments are already rejected by
115	// the guard itself.
116	//
117	// "restore" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in its terminal segment
118	// position (the fourth segment, index 3); a session or document identifier
119	// literally named "restore" occupies an identifier position (index 0 or 2) and
120	// is therefore left to the ordinary session routes like any other id.
121	func malformedSessionRestorePath(p string) bool {
122		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
123		if !ok {
124			return false
125		}
126		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
127		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
128		// has its own guard; "restore" there is an ordinary identifier, not the
129		// restore keyword.
130		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
131			return false
132		}
133		for i, seg := range segs {
134			if seg != "restore" {
135				continue
136			}
137			// Identifier positions: sessionId (0) and documentId (2). A value of
138			// "restore" there is an ordinary identifier, not the endpoint word.
139			if i == 0 || i == 2 {
140				continue
141			}
142			// Endpoint keyword position: the fourth segment must be exactly
143			// "restore" with the documents scaffolding around it, and no segment
144			// may follow. Any other occurrence is a malformed path.
145			if i == 3 && len(segs) == 4 &&
146				segs[0] != "" &&
147				segs[1] == "documents" &&
148				segs[2] != "" {
149				return false
150			}
151			return true
152		}
153		return false
154	}

14	// snapshotExportItem is one element of an export body. The struct field order
15	// fixes the on-the-wire key order to cursor then state; State is embedded as
16	// raw JSON so the stored content is emitted verbatim, exactly as the single
17	// snapshot read emits it.
18	type snapshotExportItem struct {
19		Cursor int64           `json:"cursor"`
20		State  json.RawMessage `json:"state"`
21	}
22	
23	// snapshotExportResponse is the export body with the top-level key order fixed
24	// to snapshots then count. Snapshots is always a non-nil slice so an empty
25	// export serializes as [] rather than null.
26	type snapshotExportResponse struct {
27		Snapshots []snapshotExportItem `json:"snapshots"`
28		Count     int                  `json:"count"`
29	}
30	
31	// handleExportSnapshots is the read-only batch export over a document's
32	// snapshot collection:
33	//
34	//	GET /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots?from=0&to=N
35	//
36	// from defaults to 0; to absent means no upper bound. Only snapshots whose
37	// cursor is in the closed [from, to] interval are returned, in ascending
38	// cursor order, at most one entry per cursor. An unknown document or a range
39	// without any snapshot is a successful 200 with an empty list and count 0, not
40	// an error. The handler writes nothing: it creates no snapshot, moves no
41	// cursor, records no change and notifies the push channels.
42	func handleExportSnapshots(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
43		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
44	
45		from, to, ok := parseExportInterval(w, r.URL.Query())
46		if !ok {
47			return
48		}
49	
50		snaps, err := s.ExportSnapshots(documentID, from, to)
51		if err != nil {
52			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to export snapshots")
53			return
54		}
55		writeSnapshotExport(w, snaps)
56	}
57	
58	// writeSnapshotExport renders an export result in the shared response shape: a
59	// single compact JSON line with the snapshots,count key order, each item
60	// keyed cursor,state, an empty export serializing as [] with count 0. It is
61	// shared by the document-scoped and session-scoped exports so their bodies
62	// cannot drift apart.
63	func writeSnapshotExport(w http.ResponseWriter, snaps []events.ExportedSnapshot) {
64		items := make([]snapshotExportItem, 0, len(snaps))
65		for _, snap := range snaps {
66			items = append(items, snapshotExportItem{Cursor: snap.Cursor, State: snap.State})
67		}
68		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, snapshotExportResponse{Snapshots: items, Count: len(items)})
69	}

71	// handleSessionExportSnapshots is the session-scoped view of the snapshot
72	// batch export, over the session document-read prefix with the resource
73	// segment swapped to the snapshot collection:
74	//
75	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/snapshots?from=0&to=N
76	//
77	// The interval semantics and the response body are identical to the
78	// document-level export; the path offers no other read form, so every GET is
79	// the export (from/to absent means the default interval). Around the export
80	// sit the session view's checks in their fixed order — request shape and
81	// parameters (400), session existence (404), the session device's document
82	// permission (403) — so a rejected export exposes no snapshot content and
83	// writes nothing.
84	func handleSessionExportSnapshots(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
85		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
86		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
87	
88		// Malformed interval parameters are a request-shape error (400) checked
89		// before the resource lookup (404), matching the session change export's
90		// ordering.
91		from, to, ok := parseExportInterval(w, r.URL.Query())
92		if !ok {
93			return
94		}
95	
96		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
97		if err != nil {
98			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
99				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
100				return
101			}
102			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
103			return
104		}
105	
106		authorized, err := s.DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID)
107		if err != nil {
108			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up permission")
109			return
110		}
111		if !authorized {
112			writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
113			return
114		}
115	
116		snaps, err := s.ExportSnapshots(documentID, from, to)
117		if err != nil {
118			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to export snapshots")
119			return
120		}
121		writeSnapshotExport(w, snaps)
122	}

124	// malformedSnapshotPath reports whether p targets the snapshot namespace but
125	// is not at one of its exact locations:
126	//
127	//	GET  /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots                    (the batch export)
128	//	GET  /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots/{cursor}          (the single read)
129	//	*    /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots/versions          (named versions)
130	//	*    /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots/versions/{name}
131	//	POST /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots/versions/{name}/restore
132	//
133	// A trailing slash (an empty cursor or name segment, including the collection
134	// path with a trailing slash), extra path segments, or a "snapshots" segment
135	// in any keyword position short of one of those shapes is a malformed 400
136	// rather than ServeMux's redirect or plain-text 404/405: the snapshot
137	// endpoints promise a JSON error and never a redirect. Empty segments are
138	// already rejected by the guard itself. The keyword is matched only past the
139	// documentID position, so a document literally named "snapshots" keeps its
140	// ordinary routes.
141	func malformedSnapshotPath(p string) bool {
142		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/documents/")
143		if !ok {
144			return false
145		}
146		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
147		for i, seg := range segs {
148			if seg != "snapshots" || i == 0 {
149				continue
150			}
151			// Keyword position reached. The collection is exactly
152			// {documentID}/snapshots; the single read adds one non-empty cursor
153			// segment; the named-version subtree adds the versions collection, one
154			// non-empty name segment, and optionally a trailing restore segment.
155			// Anything else (trailing slash, missing/extra segments) is malformed.
156			collection := len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] != ""
157			cursorItem := len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[2] != ""
158			versionsCollection := len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[2] == "versions"
159			versionsItem := len(segs) == 4 && segs[0] != "" && segs[2] == "versions" && segs[3] != ""
160			versionsRestore := len(segs) == 5 && segs[0] != "" && segs[2] == "versions" && segs[3] != "" && segs[4] == "restore"
161			return !(collection || cursorItem || versionsCollection || versionsItem || versionsRestore)
162		}
163		return false
164	}
165	
166	// malformedSessionSnapshotsPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped
167	// snapshot collection's shape but is not the collection's exact location
168	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/snapshots): extra path
169	// segments past the collection (the session view has no single-snapshot
170	// item, so a trailing cursor segment is malformed too). ServeMux would answer
171	// those with a plain-text 404; the snapshot surface promises a JSON 400 and
172	// never a redirect. Empty segments (doubled slashes, a trailing slash) are
173	// already rejected by the guard itself.
174	//
175	// "snapshots" is treated as the collection keyword only in the fourth
176	// segment, right after the document identifier; a session or document
177	// identifier literally named "snapshots" occupies an identifier position and
178	// keeps its ordinary routes.
179	func malformedSessionSnapshotsPath(p string) bool {
180		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
181		if !ok {
182			return false
183		}
184		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
185		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
186		// has its own guard; "snapshots" there is an ordinary identifier, not
187		// this collection's keyword.
188		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
189			return false
190		}
191		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[1] != "documents" || segs[3] != "snapshots" {
192			return false
193		}
194		// Keyword position reached. The collection is exactly
195		// {sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/snapshots; anything past it is a
196		// malformed 400.
197		return !(len(segs) == 4 && segs[0] != "" && segs[2] != "")
198	}

625	// emptyIDGuard rejects requests carrying an empty path identifier with a 400
626	// JSON error instead of letting ServeMux emit its HTML redirect or a
627	// plain-text 404.
628	//
629	// The document family keeps its original rule (an empty documentID, i.e. the
630	// prefix /v1/documents//); other odd paths there retain their old response so
631	// the pre-existing surface is unchanged. The new device/session families are
632	// stricter: any doubled slash (an empty deviceId, sessionId or documentId
633	// segment) or a trailing slash (an empty final id) is a 400 JSON error.
634	func emptyIDGuard(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
635		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
636			p := r.URL.Path
637	
638			documentSegmentEmpty := strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/documents//")
639			newFamilySegmentEmpty := false
640			if strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/devices/") || strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/") {
641				newFamilySegmentEmpty = strings.Contains(p, "//") || strings.HasSuffix(p, "/")
642			}
643	
644			if documentSegmentEmpty || newFamilySegmentEmpty || malformedDocumentDelete(r.Method, p) || malformedNewDocumentPath(p) || malformedSubscribePath(p) || malformedSessionCRDTPath(p) || malformedCRDTPath(p) || malformedSnapshotPath(p) || malformedPermissionPath(p) || malformedChangeExportPath(p) || malformedChangeQueryPath(p) || malformedSessionChangesPath(p) || malformedSessionPollPath(p) || malformedSessionReplayPath(p) || malformedSessionMergePath(p) || malformedSessionCompactPath(p) || malformedSessionQueryPath(p) || malformedSessionSnapshotsPath(p) || malformedSessionRestorePath(p) {
645				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "path identifiers must be non-empty strings")
646				return
647			}
648			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
649		})
650	}

652	// malformedNewDocumentPath reports whether p targets one of the new
653	// long-poll/replay/merge/restore/compaction endpoints but is not that
654	// endpoint's exact location: a missing/empty segment, a trailing slash, extra
655	// segments, or a "poll"/"replay"/"merge"/"restore"/"compact" segment in a
656	// position short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer those with a
657	// 301 redirect or a plain-text 404/405; the new endpoints promise a JSON error
658	// and never a redirect, so every such path is a malformed 400.
659	//
660	// Keywords are matched only past the documentID position, so documents that
661	// happen to be named "poll", "replay", "merge", "restore" or "compact" keep
662	// their ordinary merge/snapshot/changes routes.
663	func malformedNewDocumentPath(p string) bool {
664		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/documents/")
665		if !ok {
666			return false
667		}
668		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
669	
670		// The named-snapshot-version subtree ({documentID}/snapshots/versions/...)
671		// owns its whole shape verdict through malformedSnapshotPath. A version
672		// name may coincide with a change keyword ("poll", "merge", "restore",
673		// "subscribe", "compact"), so none of the keyword loops below may judge a
674		// path inside that subtree; leave it to the snapshot guard.
675		if len(segs) >= 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "snapshots" && segs[2] == "versions" {
676			return false
677		}
678	
679		// Poll endpoint: "poll" must be exactly the third segment, after a
680		// non-empty documentID and "changes".
681		for i, seg := range segs {
682			if seg == "poll" && i > 0 {
683				return !(len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "changes")
684			}
685		}
686		// Document change subscription: "subscribe" must be exactly the third
687		// segment, after a non-empty documentID and "changes". The CRDT namespace
688		// has its own state/subscribe endpoint and its own guard, so a "subscribe"
689		// under crdt/ is not the change-subscription keyword.
690		for i, seg := range segs {
691			if seg == "subscribe" && i > 0 {
692				if len(segs) >= 2 && segs[1] == "crdt" {
693					continue
694				}
695				return !(len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "changes")
696			}
697		}
698		// Replay endpoint: "replay" must be exactly the second segment, after a
699		// non-empty documentID.
700		for i, seg := range segs {
701			if seg == "replay" && i > 0 {
702				return !(len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] != "")
703			}
704		}
705		// Merge and restore endpoints: each keyword must be exactly the second
706		// segment, after a non-empty documentID (they are document-item
707		// subresources, unlike poll/compact which sit below the change
708		// collection). A keyword used as a version name inside the versions
709		// subtree was excluded by the early return above.
710		for _, keyword := range []string{"merge", "restore"} {
711			for i, seg := range segs {
712				if seg == keyword && i > 0 {
713					return !(len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] != "")
714				}
715			}
716		}
717		// Compaction endpoint: "compact" must be exactly the third segment, after
718		// a non-empty documentID and "changes". The CRDT namespace has its own
719		// guard; "compact" there is the CRDT compaction keyword, not the
720		// change-log one.
721		for i, seg := range segs {
722			if seg == "compact" && i > 0 {
723				if len(segs) >= 2 && segs[1] == "crdt" {
724					return false
725				}
726				return !(len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "changes")
727			}
728		}
729		return false
730	}

732	// malformedSubscribePath reports whether p targets the WebSocket subscription
733	// endpoint but is not at its exact location
734	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes/subscribe): a
735	// missing "documents"/"changes" segment, an extra segment, or a "subscribe"
736	// segment short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer those with a
737	// plain-text 404/405; every failure of this endpoint must be a JSON 400
738	// instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the guard itself.
739	//
740	// "subscribe" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the endpoint's
741	// terminal segment position (the fifth segment, index 4); a session or
742	// document identifier literally named "subscribe" occupies an identifier
743	// position (index 0 or 2) and is therefore left to the ordinary
744	// changes/subscribe routes like any other id.
745	func malformedSubscribePath(p string) bool {
746		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
747		if !ok {
748			return false
749		}
750		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
751		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
752		// has its own guard; "subscribe" there is not the changes-subscribe
753		// keyword.
754		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
755			return false
756		}
757		for i, seg := range segs {
758			if seg != "subscribe" {
759				continue
760			}
761			// Identifier positions: sessionId (0) and documentId (2). A value of
762			// "subscribe" there is an ordinary identifier, not the endpoint word.
763			if i == 0 || i == 2 {
764				continue
765			}
766			// Endpoint keyword position: the fifth segment must be exactly
767			// "subscribe" with the documents/changes scaffolding around it, and no
768			// segment may follow. Any other occurrence is a malformed path.
769			if i == 4 && len(segs) == 5 &&
770				segs[0] != "" &&
771				segs[1] == "documents" &&
772				segs[2] != "" &&
773				segs[3] == "changes" {
774				return false
775			}
776			return true
777		}
778		return false
779	}

781	// malformedSessionCRDTPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped CRDT
782	// namespace but is not at one of its four exact locations:
783	//
784	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/ops
785	//	GET  /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state
786	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/compact
787	//	GET  /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state/subscribe
788	//
789	// a missing "ops"/"state"/"compact"/"subscribe" segment, an extra segment, or
790	// a "crdt" segment in the keyword position (immediately past the document
791	// identifier) short of one of the registered shapes. ServeMux would answer
792	// those with a plain-text 404/405; every failure of these endpoints must be a
793	// JSON 400 instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the guard itself.
794	//
795	// "crdt" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the fourth segment (index
796	// 3, right after the document identifier); a session or document identifier
797	// literally named "crdt" occupies an identifier position (index 0 or 2) and
798	// keeps its ordinary routes. Likewise "compact" is the endpoint keyword only
799	// in the fifth segment; a session or document literally named "compact" is an
800	// ordinary identifier.
801	func malformedSessionCRDTPath(p string) bool {
802		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
803		if !ok {
804			return false
805		}
806		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
807		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[1] != "documents" || segs[3] != "crdt" {
808			return false
809		}
810		// Keyword position reached. The batch commit, the state read and the
811		// compaction are all exactly
812		// {sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/{ops,state,compact}; the
813		// subscription adds one trailing "subscribe" segment.
814		validOps := len(segs) == 5 &&
815			segs[0] != "" &&
816			segs[2] != "" &&
817			segs[4] == "ops"
818		validState := len(segs) == 5 &&
819			segs[0] != "" &&
820			segs[2] != "" &&
821			segs[4] == "state"
822		validCompact := len(segs) == 5 &&
823			segs[0] != "" &&
824			segs[2] != "" &&
825			segs[4] == "compact"
826		validSubscribe := len(segs) == 6 &&
827			segs[0] != "" &&
828			segs[2] != "" &&
829			segs[4] == "state" &&
830			segs[5] == "subscribe"
831		return !(validOps || validState || validCompact || validSubscribe)
832	}

844	// decodeJSONBody enforces the strict POST contract shared by every JSON
845	// endpoint: Content-Type must be application/json, the body is capped at
846	// maxBatchBytes, it must contain exactly one JSON value, and no trailing data
847	// may follow it. Any violation writes a 400 JSON error and returns false; the
848	// caller returns immediately, so no handler reaches the store with malformed
849	// input and rejected requests write nothing.
850	func decodeJSONBody(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, dst any) bool {
851		mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
852		if err != nil || mediaType != "application/json" {
853			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Content-Type must be application/json")
854			return false
855		}
856	
857		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBatchBytes)
858		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
859		if err := dec.Decode(dst); err != nil {
860			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: "+err.Error())
861			return false
862		}
863		// Reject trailing data after the JSON value.
864		if err := dec.Decode(&struct{}{}); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
865			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: unexpected trailing content")
866			return false
867		}
868		return true
869	}

1293		}

1301	// parseNonNegativeInt reports whether raw is a JSON integer >= 0. Floats,// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
1302	func parseNonNegativeInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
1303		var n int64
1304		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &n); err != nil || n < 0 {
1305			return 0, false
1306		}
1307		// Guard against values like 1.0 that Unmarshal into int64 on some inputs;
1308		// require the literal to contain no fraction or exponent.
1309		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(raw))
1310		if trimmed == "" || trimmed[0] == '-' {
1311			return 0, false
1312		}
1313		for _, c := range trimmed {
1314			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
1315				return 0, false
1316			}
1317		}
1318		return n, true
1319	}

1321	// parsePositiveInt reports whether raw is a JSON integer >= 1. Zero, floats,
1322	// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
1323	func parsePositiveInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
1324		n, ok := parseNonNegativeInt(raw)
1325		if !ok || n < 1 {
1326			return 0, false
1327		}
1328		return n, true
1329	}

1332	// array or a scalar).
1333	func isJSONObject(raw json.RawMessage) bool {

1335		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &m); err != nil || m == nil {
1336			return false
1337		}
1338		return true

1423	// handleSessionPostChanges is the session-scoped batch commit over the same
1424	// change collection the session reads page:
1425	//
1426	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes
1427	//
1428	// The request body carries only the changes array — the calling device is the
1429	// session's owning device, resolved with the same identity rule as the
1430	// session reads, exports and subscriptions; no new credential is introduced
1431	// and no device id travels in the body. Per-element semantics and the success
1432	// body are byte-identical to the document-level commit: results arrive in
1433	// request order, each naming its id, whether it was created and the cursor it
1434	// was assigned. The checks run in the fixed order request shape (400),
1435	// session existence (404), document permission (403) — the permission verdict
1436	// is taken inside the commit transaction, so a revoked device writes nothing —
1437	// and a payload/device mismatch against an existing id is a 409 reporting the
1438	// conflicting id. Every rejection leaves the log untouched.

1446		}

1448			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "changes must be a non-empty array")
1449			return
1450		}

1454		for i, c := range req.Changes {
1455			if c.ID == "" {
1456				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must have a non-empty string id")
1457				return
1458			}
1459			if len(c.Payload) == 0 {
1460				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must carry a JSON payload")
1461				return
1462			}
1463			if _, dup := seen[c.ID]; dup {
1464				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate change id within batch: "+c.ID)
1465				return
1466			}
1467			seen[c.ID] = struct{}{}

1469		}

1516	//
1517	// The body carries only the operations array in original order, each with a
1518	// stable id and any legal JSON payload; the calling device is the session's
1519	// owning device resolved from the path with the same identity rule as the
1520	// session reads, exports, commits, polls and subscriptions — no new credential
1521	// is introduced, and a stray deviceId in the body is ignored like any other
1522	// unknown field. Per-element semantics and the success body are
1523	// byte-identical to the document-level replay: results arrive in request
1524	// order, each naming its id, whether it was created and the first cursor it
1525	// was (or had been) assigned. The checks run in the fixed order request
1526	// shape (400), session existence (404), document permission (403) — the
1527	// permission verdict is taken inside the commit transaction, so a revoked
1528	// device writes nothing — and an id whose payload or source device differs
1529	// from the stored row is a 409 reporting the conflicting id. Every
1530	// rejection leaves the log untouched.
1531	func handleSessionReplay(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {

1533		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty

1540			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "operations must be a non-empty array")
1541			return
1542		}
1543		if len(req.Operations) == 0 {
1544			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "operations must be a non-empty array")
1545			return
1546		}
1547	
1548		changes := make([]events.Change, len(req.Operations))
1549		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Operations))
1550		for i, op := range req.Operations {
1551			if op.ID == "" {
1552				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each operation must have a non-empty string id")
1553				return
1554			}
1555			if len(op.Payload) == 0 {
1556				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each operation must carry a JSON payload")
1557				return
1558			}
1559			if _, dup := seen[op.ID]; dup {
1560				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate operation id within batch: "+op.ID)
1561				return
1562			}
1563			seen[op.ID] = struct{}{}
1564			changes[i] = events.Change{ID: op.ID, Payload: op.Payload}
1565		}
1566	
1567		// Request shape is settled; only now does the session lookup run, so a
1568		// malformed batch against an unknown session is still a 400.
1569		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
1570		if err != nil {
1571			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
1572				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1573				return
1574			}
1575			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
1576			return
1577		}
1578		for i := range changes {
1579			changes[i].DeviceID = deviceID
1580		}
1581	
1582		results, err := s.ReplaySessionChanges(documentID, changes)
1583		if err != nil {
1584			var conflict *events.ErrConflict
1585			switch {
1586			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
1587				// The session's device was deregistered between the lookup and
1588				// the commit; its cascade removed the session too, so the
1589				// identity the caller used no longer exists.
1590				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1591			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
1592				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1593			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
1594				writeJSON(w, http.StatusConflict, map[string]string{
1595					"error":      "operation id already exists with different deviceId or payload",
1596					"conflictId": conflict.ID,
1597				})
1598			default:
1599				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to replay operations")
1600			}
1601			return
1602		}
1603	
1604		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"results": results})
1605	}

1607	// sessionMergeRequest is the session-scoped merge body: only the observed base
1608	// cursor and the single change travel in the request. The calling device is the
1609	// session's owning device resolved from the path, so a stray deviceId is
1610	// decoded and ignored like every other unknown field.
1611	type sessionMergeRequest struct {
1612		BaseCursor json.RawMessage `json:"baseCursor"`
1613		Change     *mergeChangeIn  `json:"change"`
1614	}
1615	
1616	// handleSessionMergeChange is the session-scoped single-change merge entry,
1617	// the session view's counterpart to
1618	// POST /v1/documents/{documentID}/merge, mounted one segment below the change
1619	// collection:
1620	//
1621	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes/merge
1622	//
1623	// The body carries only baseCursor and one change; the calling device is the
1624	// session's owning device resolved from the path with the same identity rule as
1625	// the session reads, exports, commits, replays, polls and subscriptions — no
1626	// new credential is introduced, and a stray deviceId in the body is ignored
1627	// like any other unknown field. The merge judgment, success body and cursor
1628	// space are byte-identical to the document-level merge: a single result naming
1629	// the id, its three-way outcome ("applied", "merged" or "idempotent") and the
1630	// cursor it received, with the original result attached only when nothing was
1631	// created. The checks run in the fixed order request shape (400), session
1632	// existence (404), document permission (403) — the permission verdict is taken
1633	// inside the merge transaction, so a revoked device writes nothing — and the
1634	// in-transaction merge failures (a stale or compacted base cursor, an
1635	// id/payload/source mismatch, a key collision or a non-object later payload)
1636	// answer 400 or 409 with zero writes.
1637	func handleSessionMergeChange(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1638		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1639		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1640	
1641		var req sessionMergeRequest
1642		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
1643			return
1644		}
1645		// baseCursor must be present and a non-negative integer (no fractions,
1646		// strings, booleans or null).
1647		if len(req.BaseCursor) == 0 {
1648			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "baseCursor must be a non-negative integer")
1649			return
1650		}
1651		baseCursor, ok := parseNonNegativeInt(req.BaseCursor)
1652		if !ok {
1653			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "baseCursor must be a non-negative integer")
1654			return
1655		}
1656		if req.Change == nil {
1657			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "change must be an object")
1658			return
1659		}
1660		if req.Change.ID == "" {
1661			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "change.id must be a non-empty string")
1662			return
1663		}
1664		if len(req.Change.Payload) == 0 || !isJSONObject(req.Change.Payload) {
1665			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "change.payload must be a JSON object")
1666			return
1667		}
1668	
1669		// Request shape is settled; only now does the session lookup run, so a
1670		// malformed merge against an unknown session is still a 400.
1671		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
1672		if err != nil {
1673			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
1674				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1675				return
1676			}
1677			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
1678			return
1679		}
1680	
1681		result, err := s.MergeSessionChange(documentID, baseCursor, events.Change{
1682			ID:       req.Change.ID,
1683			DeviceID: deviceID,
1684			Payload:  req.Change.Payload,
1685		})
1686		if err != nil {
1687			var conflict *events.ErrConflict
1688			switch {
1689			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
1690				// The session's device was deregistered between the lookup and the
1691				// merge; its cascade removed the session too, so the identity the
1692				// caller used no longer exists.
1693				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1694			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
1695				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1696			case errors.Is(err, events.ErrStaleCursor):
1697				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "baseCursor is unknown or greater than the current cursor")
1698			case errors.Is(err, events.ErrCompactedBase):
1699				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "baseCursor is below the compaction boundary")
1700			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
1701				writeJSON(w, http.StatusConflict, map[string]string{
1702					"error":      "merge conflicts with existing changes",
1703					"conflictId": conflict.ID,
1704				})
1705			default:
1706				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to merge change")
1707			}
1708			return
1709		}
1710	
1711		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, result)
1712	}

1714	// parseChangesQuery parses the shared after/limit pagination parameters,
1715	// writing the documented 400 on an illegal value. It is shared by the
1716	// document-scoped and session-scoped change listings so their query semantics
1717	// cannot drift apart.
1718	func parseChangesQuery(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (after, limit int64, ok bool) {
1719		q := r.URL.Query()
1720	
1721		after = 0
1722		if raw := q.Get("after"); raw != "" {
1723			v, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
1724			if err != nil || v < 0 {
1725				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "after must be a non-negative integer")
1726				return 0, 0, false
1727			}
1728			after = v
1729		}
1730	
1731		limit = defaultListLimit
1732		if raw := q.Get("limit"); raw != "" {
1733			v, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
1734			if err != nil || v < 1 || v > maxListLimit {
1735				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "limit must be an integer between 1 and 1000")
1736				return 0, 0, false
1737			}
1738			limit = v
1739		}
1740	
1741		return after, limit, true
1742	}
1743	
1744	// writeChangesPage renders a change listing page in the shared response shape.
1745	func writeChangesPage(w http.ResponseWriter, changes []events.ListedChange, nextCursor int64) {
1746		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
1747			"changes":    changes,
1748			"nextCursor": nextCursor,
1749		})
1750	}
1751	
1752	// parsePollWaitMs parses the long-poll waitMs query parameter, writing the
1753	// documented 400 on an illegal value. It accepts an integer in 0..30000
1754	// milliseconds and defaults to 0 when the parameter is absent; a value outside
1755	// the range, a fraction, an exponent or any non-numeric value is rejected. It
1756	// is shared by the document-scoped and session-scoped long polls so their wait
1757	// semantics cannot drift apart.
1758	func parsePollWaitMs(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (int64, bool) {
1759		var waitMs int64
1760		if raw := r.URL.Query().Get("waitMs"); raw != "" {
1761			v, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
1762			if err != nil || v < 0 || v > maxPollWaitMillis {
1763				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "waitMs must be an integer between 0 and 30000")
1764				return 0, false
1765			}
1766			waitMs = v
1767		}
1768		return waitMs, true
1769	}
1770	
1771	// writePollPage renders a long-poll result in the shared response shape: the
1772	// ordinary page plus a timedOut flag, with the top-level keys in the fixed
1773	// changes, nextCursor, timedOut order.
1774	func writePollPage(w http.ResponseWriter, changes []events.ListedChange, nextCursor int64, timedOut bool) {
1775		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
1776			"changes":    changes,
1777			"nextCursor": nextCursor,
1778			"timedOut":   timedOut,
1779		})
1780	}
1781	
1782	func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
1783		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
1784		w.WriteHeader(status)
1785		_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
1786	}
1787	
1788	func writeError(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, message string) {
1789		writeJSON(w, status, map[string]string{"error": message})
1790	}

1792	// handlePollChanges is the long-polling entry over the change log.
1793	//
1794	// Query params share the existing change-read constraints: after is a
1795	// non-negative cursor (default 0) and limit is 1..1000 (default 100); waitMs
1796	// is 0..30000 (default 0). Rows already past after return immediately; a known
1797	// document caught up to after parks until the first new commit or the wait
1798	// deadline; an unknown document returns an empty page with cursor 0 at once.
1799	// The response shape is the ordinary page plus a timedOut flag; a deadline
1800	// expiry echoes the caller's cursor and never advances it. A client
1801	// disconnect simply stops the wait and writes nothing.
1802	func handlePollChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1803		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1804	
1805		after, limit, ok := parseChangesQuery(w, r)
1806		if !ok {
1807			return
1808		}
1809		waitMs, ok := parsePollWaitMs(w, r)
1810		if !ok {
1811			return
1812		}
1813	
1814		changes, nextCursor, timedOut, err := s.WaitForChanges(
1815			r.Context(), documentID, after, limit, time.Duration(waitMs)*time.Millisecond,
1816		)
1817		switch {
1818		case errors.Is(err, events.ErrStoreClosing):
1819			writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "service is shutting down")
1820			return
1821		case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled), errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
1822			// The client went away (or, with waitMs bounded, its deadline lapsed
1823			// at the transport): nothing more to write and nothing was stored.
1824			return
1825		case err != nil:
1826			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to poll changes")
1827			return
1828		}
1829	
1830		writePollPage(w, changes, nextCursor, timedOut)
1831	}
1832	
1833	// handleSessionPollChanges is the session-scoped long-poll continuation over
1834	// the same change collection the session reads page:
1835	//
1836	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes/poll
1837	//
1838	// The request is a GET with no body; the calling device is the session's
1839	// owning device resolved with the same identity rule as the session reads,
1840	// exports, commits and subscriptions. Query parameters and the success body are
1841	// identical to GET /v1/documents/{documentID}/changes/poll — after (default 0),
1842	// limit (default 100, 1..1000) and waitMs (default 0, 0..30000), answered with
1843	// changes, nextCursor and timedOut in that order, rows ascending by cursor.
1844	//
1845	// Rows already past after return immediately with timedOut=false; a known
1846	// document caught up to after parks until the first commit through any write
1847	// path (session batch commit, document commit, merge, restore, replay) or the
1848	// wait deadline; an unknown document returns an empty page with cursor 0 at
1849	// once and never parks. A deadline expiry returns the empty page, echoes the
1850	// caller's after and sets timedOut=true without advancing the cursor. Checks
1851	// run in the fixed order request shape and parameters (400), session
1852	// existence (404), document permission (403); a rejected request exposes no
1853	// change content. A client disconnect simply cancels the wait and writes
1854	// nothing; while the service is shutting down the parked request answers a
1855	// JSON 503.
1856	func handleSessionPollChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1857		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1858		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1859	
1860		// Parameter shape precedes the session lookup, matching the session paged
1861		// read's ordering: a malformed after/limit/waitMs against an unknown
1862		// session is still a 400.
1863		after, limit, ok := parseChangesQuery(w, r)
1864		if !ok {
1865			return
1866		}
1867		waitMs, ok := parsePollWaitMs(w, r)
1868		if !ok {
1869			return
1870		}
1871	
1872		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
1873		if err != nil {
1874			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
1875				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1876				return
1877			}
1878			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
1879			return
1880		}
1881	
1882		authorized, err := s.DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID)
1883		if err != nil {
1884			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up permission")
1885			return
1886		}
1887		if !authorized {
1888			writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1889			return
1890		}
1891	
1892		changes, nextCursor, timedOut, err := s.WaitForChanges(
1893			r.Context(), documentID, after, limit, time.Duration(waitMs)*time.Millisecond,
1894		)
1895		switch {
1896		case errors.Is(err, events.ErrStoreClosing):
1897			writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "service is shutting down")
1898			return
1899		case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled), errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
1900			// The client went away (or, with waitMs bounded, its deadline lapsed
1901			// at the transport): nothing more to write and nothing was stored.
1902			return
1903		case err != nil:
1904			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to poll changes")
1905			return
1906		}
1907	
1908		writePollPage(w, changes, nextCursor, timedOut)
1909	}
1910	
1911	// handleReplay retries an offline batch against the existing change log. The
1912	// request and per-element semantics mirror POST .../changes — strict
1913	// application/json body, non-empty ids, no in-batch duplicates, idempotent only
1914	// when deviceId and decoded payload match, otherwise 409 reporting the
1915	// conflicting id — with the registration/permission layer enforced first:
1916	// 404 for an unregistered device and 403 for a revoked one, neither exposing
1917	// change content. The whole batch commits in one serialized transaction that
1918	// shares the document's contiguous cursor space with ordinary commits.
1919	func handleReplay(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1920		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1921	
1922		var req replayRequest
1923		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
1924			return
1925		}
1926		if req.DeviceID == "" {
1927			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
1928			return
1929		}
1930		if req.Operations == nil {
1931			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "operations must be a non-empty array")
1932			return
1933		}
1934		if len(req.Operations) == 0 {
1935			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "operations must be a non-empty array")
1936			return
1937		}
1938	
1939		changes := make([]events.Change, len(req.Operations))
1940		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Operations))

1943				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each operation must have a non-empty string id")
1944				return
1945			}

1949			}

1953			}
1954			seen[op.ID] = struct{}{}
1955			changes[i] = events.Change{ID: op.ID, DeviceID: req.DeviceID, Payload: op.Payload}
1956		}
1957	
1958		results, err := s.ReplayChanges(documentID, changes)
1959		if err != nil {
1960			var conflict *events.ErrConflict
1961			switch {
1962			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
1963				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
1964			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
1965				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")

1967				writeJSON(w, http.StatusConflict, map[string]string{
1968					"error":      "operation id already exists with different deviceId or payload",
1969					"conflictId": conflict.ID,
1970				})

1972				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to replay operations")

1	// Package app is the composition root: it opens the one shared database and
2	// constructs the three independently reusable internal services — the change
3	// event service, the permission service and the CRDT state service — wiring
4	// them together only through their internal interfaces.
5	//
6	// The services share one SQLite connection (the kernel opens a single
7	// pooled connection with immediate transactions), so a change commit, a CRDT
8	// submission or compaction, and a permission change are serialized on the
9	// same connection and leave no half-written batch. The change event and CRDT
10	// services take their registration-and-authorization verdict from the
11	// permission service inside their own transactions (events.Gate / crdt.Gate),
12	// and the permission service fans a committed revoke out to their
13	// subscription registries through authz.RevokeSink. No service reaches into
14	// another service's tables or fields.
15	//
16	// App is the single object the entry and HTTP layers use. It promotes each
17	// service's input/output boundary as its methods while hiding the wiring; it
18	// adds no authentication and exposes no endpoint of its own.
19	package app
20	
21	import (
22		"context"
23		"encoding/json"
24		"time"
25	
26		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/authz"
27		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/crdt"
28		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/events"
29		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/push"
30		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
31	)
32	
33	// App composes the durable kernel and the three internal services over one
34	// shared database connection.
35	type App struct {
36		*store.Store
37	
38		events *events.Service
39		crdt   *crdt.Service
40	
41		// pushSubs is the process-wide, in-memory registry of the live push
42		// connections across both channels. It backs the device-scoped
43		// subscription management endpoints and holds no durable state.
44		pushSubs *push.Registry
45	
46		// Authz is the permission service. It is exposed so the HTTP layer can
47		// grant/revoke and read authorization directly; the other services reach
48		// it through their gates rather than this field.
49		Authz *authz.Service
50	}
51	
52	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path and constructs
53	// every internal service over it. The empty path opens a private in-memory
54	// database useful for tests. A construction failure closes the kernel and
55	// leaves nothing behind.
56	func Open(path string) (*App, error) {
57		kernel, err := store.Open(path)
58		if err != nil {
59			return nil, err
60		}
61	
62		// The permission service is built first: its gate is a constructor
63		// dependency of the change event and CRDT services.
64		permissions, err := authz.New(kernel)
65		if err != nil {
66			_ = kernel.Close()
67			return nil, err
68		}
69		eventService, err := events.New(kernel, permissions)
70		if err != nil {
71			_ = kernel.Close()
72			return nil, err
73		}
74		crdtService, err := crdt.New(kernel, permissions)
75		if err != nil {
76			_ = kernel.Close()
77			return nil, err
78		}
79	
80		// A committed revoke ends the affected live subscriptions in both
81		// push channels. The dependency is an interface, registered once here, so
82		// the permission service never names either subscriber concretely.
83		permissions.AddRevokeSink(eventsRevokeSink{eventService})

335	// DeleteDocument removes a registered device's whole document in one
336	// serialized, synchronously committed transaction. The calling device is

340	//
341	//   - an unregistered device yields store.ErrDeviceNotFound (404) and writes
342	//     nothing;
343	//   - a device whose permission for the document was revoked yields
344	//     store.ErrPermissionDenied (403) and no cleanup runs;
345	//   - a document with no durable data anywhere — never created or already
346	//     deleted — yields events.ErrDocumentNotFound (404) and writes nothing.
347	//

349	// and trimmed change log, the retained idempotency summaries, its snapshots
350	// and named snapshot-version markers, its CRDT state and the per-document
351	// permission ledger. The same id is a brand-new document afterward — the
352	// cursor space restarts at 1 — and inherits no history or version names.

354	// the deletions share one immediate transaction on the single connection.

357	// ended (close code 4420 on both push channels) and dropped from the

367		// Registration first, then permission, both before any document content
368		// is observed: a rejected delete reveals nothing and cleans nothing.
369		if err := a.Authz.AuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID); err != nil {
370			return err
371		}
372	
373		eventsExist, err := a.events.DocumentDataExistsTx(tx, documentID)
374		if err != nil {
375			return err
376		}
377		crdtExist, err := a.crdt.DocumentDataExistsTx(tx, documentID)
378		if err != nil {
379			return err
380		}
381		// A ledger-only deviation row also counts as document data, so a document
382		// whose only durable trace is a grant/revoke still deletes cleanly and the
383		// re-created id inherits no authorization state.
384		ledgerExist, err := a.Authz.DocumentHasRowsTx(tx, documentID)
385		if err != nil {
386			return err
387		}
388		if !eventsExist && !crdtExist && !ledgerExist {
389			return events.ErrDocumentNotFound
390		}
391	
392		if err := a.events.DeleteDocumentDataTx(tx, documentID); err != nil {
393			return err
394		}
395		if err := a.crdt.DeleteDocumentDataTx(tx, documentID); err != nil {
396			return err
397		}
398		if err := a.Authz.DeleteDocumentPermissionsTx(tx, documentID); err != nil {
399			return err
400		}
401	
402		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
403			return err

407		// from the management registry only after the cleanup is durable: the
408		// close is one-shot per connection, so a client re-subscribing to the
409		// now-fresh id opens a new connection and never reopens the ended ones.
410		a.events.SignalDocumentDeleted(documentID)
411		a.crdt.SignalDocumentDeleted(documentID)
412		a.CloseDocumentPush(documentID)
413		return nil
414	}

96	// of its row or not at all — never half of it. The read starts no
97	// transaction, writes nothing and notifies no waiters, so it cannot move a
98	// cursor or produce a change record.
99	func (s *Service) ExportSnapshots(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]ExportedSnapshot, error) {
100		var (
101			rows *sql.Rows
102			err  error
103		)
104		if to == nil {
105			rows, err = s.db.Query(
106				`SELECT cursor, state FROM snapshots
107				 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor >= ?
108				 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
109				documentID, from,
110			)
111		} else {
112			rows, err = s.db.Query(
113				`SELECT cursor, state FROM snapshots
114				 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor >= ? AND cursor <= ?
115				 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
116				documentID, from, *to,
117			)
118		}
119		if err != nil {
120			return nil, err
121		}
122		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
123	
124		out := make([]ExportedSnapshot, 0)
125		for rows.Next() {
126			var snap ExportedSnapshot
127			if err := rows.Scan(&snap.Cursor, &snap.State); err != nil {
128				return nil, err
129			}
130			out = append(out, snap)
131		}
132		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
133			return nil, err
134		}
135		return out, nil
136	}

138	// RestoreSnapshot appends one ordinary change whose payload is the state of
139	// documentID's snapshot at snapshotCursor, all within a single serialized
140	// transaction.
141	//
142	//   - A snapshot miss (unknown document or a cursor without a snapshot)
143	//     returns ErrSnapshotNotFound; nothing is written.
144	//   - If changeID already belongs to a prior restore, the call is idempotent
145	//     only when deviceId, snapshotCursor and the decoded source state all
146	//     match; the first result (created=false, original cursor) is returned.
147	//   - If changeID is taken by an ordinary change, or a restore whose provenance
148	//     differs, the call returns *ErrRestoreConflict; nothing is written.
149	//
150	// Otherwise a new change is appended with the next document cursor and the
151	// restore provenance is recorded. Old rows are never modified.
152	func (s *Service) RestoreSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (RestoreResult, error) {
153		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
154		if err != nil {
155			return RestoreResult{}, err
156		}
157		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
158	
159		result, err := restoreSnapshotTx(tx, documentID, deviceID, changeID, snapshotCursor)
160		if err != nil {
161			return RestoreResult{}, err
162		}
163		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
164			return RestoreResult{}, err
165		}
166		// A genuinely new restore appended a change and is the only outcome that
167		// wakes the long polls and pushes to subscribers; an idempotent repeat
168		// appended nothing and notifies nothing.
169		if result.Created {
170			s.notifyWaiters(documentID)
171		}
172		return result, nil
173	}

175	// RestoreSnapshotAuthorized is the session-scoped restore: it has exactly the
176	// restore semantics of RestoreSnapshot, but enforces the gate (registration
177	// then permission) first in the same serialized transaction: an unregistered
178	// device yields store.ErrDeviceNotFound and a revoked device yields
179	// ErrPermissionDenied. None of those outcomes writes anything or observes
180	// snapshot or change content. The device identity is resolved from the session
181	// by the HTTP layer before the call.
182	func (s *Service) RestoreSnapshotAuthorized(documentID, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (RestoreResult, error) {
183		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
184		if err != nil {
185			return RestoreResult{}, err
186		}
187		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
188	
189		// Gate first: the device row and the permission row are read before the
190		// snapshot is looked up or any change content is observed, so a rejected
191		// restore cannot reveal anything.
192		if s.gate != nil {
193			if err := s.gate.DeviceAuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID); err != nil {
194				return RestoreResult{}, err
195			}
196		}
197	
198		result, err := restoreSnapshotTx(tx, documentID, deviceID, changeID, snapshotCursor)
199		if err != nil {
200			return RestoreResult{}, err
201		}
202		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
203			return RestoreResult{}, err
204		}
205		if result.Created {
206			s.notifyWaiters(documentID)
207		}
208		return result, nil
209	}

211	// restoreSnapshotTx runs the snapshot lookup, the idempotency/conflict
212	// resolution and the single append inside the caller's serialized
213	// transaction. It is shared by the document-level restore and the
214	// session-scoped authorized restore so the two paths cannot drift: both take
215	// their snapshot miss (ErrSnapshotNotFound), conflict (*ErrRestoreConflict)
216	// and append decisions from one code path. The result's Created flag tells
217	// the caller whether a change-bearing transaction just committed and the push
218	// channels therefore need waking.
219	func restoreSnapshotTx(tx *sql.Tx, documentID, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (RestoreResult, error) {
220		// The snapshot must exist; its state is the payload to append.
221		var state []byte
222		err := tx.QueryRow(
223			`SELECT state FROM snapshots WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor = ?`,
224			documentID, snapshotCursor,
225		).Scan(&state)
226		switch {
227		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
228			return RestoreResult{}, ErrSnapshotNotFound
229		case err != nil:
230			return RestoreResult{}, err
231		}
232	
233		// Resolve the change id: an ordinary row, a prior restore and a
234		// compacted-away id's retained summary are handled differently, so consult
235		// all three.
236		var existingCursor int64
237		var existingDevice string
238		var existingPayload []byte
239		err = tx.QueryRow(
240			`SELECT cursor, device_id, payload FROM changes WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
241			documentID, changeID,
242		).Scan(&existingCursor, &existingDevice, &existingPayload)
243		switch {
244		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
245			// No online row: the id may belong to a change compaction trimmed.
246			// Its retained summary still decides — an idempotent restore needs the
247			// same device, snapshot cursor and source state; an id left by an
248			// ordinary trimmed change is a conflict, as is any mismatch.
249			var summaryDevice string
250			var summaryDigest []byte
251			var summaryCursor int64
252			var restoredFrom sql.NullInt64
253			err := tx.QueryRow(
254				`SELECT device_id, digest, cursor, restored_from FROM change_identities
255				 WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
256				documentID, changeID,
257			).Scan(&summaryDevice, &summaryDigest, &summaryCursor, &restoredFrom)
258			switch {
259			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
260				// Genuinely new id; fall through to append below.
261			case err != nil:
262				return RestoreResult{}, err
263			default:
264				stateDigest, err := payloadDigest(state)
265				if err != nil {
266					return RestoreResult{}, err
267				}
268				if !restoredFrom.Valid || restoredFrom.Int64 != snapshotCursor ||
269					summaryDevice != deviceID || !bytes.Equal(summaryDigest, stateDigest) {
270					return RestoreResult{}, &ErrRestoreConflict{ID: changeID}
271				}
272				return RestoreResult{
273					ID:           changeID,
274					Created:      false,
275					Cursor:       summaryCursor,
276					RestoredFrom: snapshotCursor,
277				}, nil
278			}
279		case err != nil:
280			return RestoreResult{}, err
281		default:
282			var restDevice string
283			var restSnapshotCursor int64
284			var restState []byte
285			err = tx.QueryRow(
286				`SELECT device_id, snapshot_cursor, state FROM restores WHERE document_id = ? AND change_id = ?`,
287				documentID, changeID,
288			).Scan(&restDevice, &restSnapshotCursor, &restState)
289			switch {
290			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
291				// The id belongs to an ordinary change (or a batch/merge change),
292				// not a restore: never treat it as an idempotent restore.
293				return RestoreResult{}, &ErrRestoreConflict{ID: changeID}
294			case err != nil:
295				return RestoreResult{}, err
296			default:
297				if restDevice != deviceID || restSnapshotCursor != snapshotCursor || !store.JSONEqual(restState, state) {
298					return RestoreResult{}, &ErrRestoreConflict{ID: changeID}
299				}
300				return RestoreResult{
301					ID:           changeID,
302					Created:      false,
303					Cursor:       existingCursor,
304					RestoredFrom: snapshotCursor,
305				}, nil
306			}
307		}
308	
309		nextCursor, err := currentCursorTx(tx, documentID)
310		if err != nil {
311			return RestoreResult{}, err
312		}
313		nextCursor++
314		if _, err := tx.Exec(
315			`INSERT INTO changes (document_id, cursor, id, device_id, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
316			documentID, nextCursor, changeID, deviceID, state,
317		); err != nil {
318			return RestoreResult{}, err
319		}
320		if _, err := tx.Exec(
321			`INSERT INTO restores (document_id, change_id, device_id, snapshot_cursor, change_cursor, state)
322			 VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
323			documentID, changeID, deviceID, snapshotCursor, nextCursor, state,
324		); err != nil {
325			return RestoreResult{}, err
326		}
327		return RestoreResult{
328			ID:           changeID,
329			Created:      true,
330			Cursor:       nextCursor,
331			RestoredFrom: snapshotCursor,
332		}, nil
333	}
